U11 NIGHT MATCH

Friday Night Lights in Niagara: Halton Cricket Academy U11s Shine in Thrilling Evening Clash

NIAGARA FALLS, ON — It was an evening filled with excitement, cheers, and invaluable cricket education as Halton Cricket Academy’s Under-11 squad traveled down the QEW to the Niagara Cricket Centre for a memorable night encounter under the floodlights against NCC Academy. While the final scorecard showed a narrow 17-run victory for the hosts, the experience gained and the electric atmosphere made it a true triumph for the young Halton side and their travelling supporters.

Stepping Under the Lights
For many of our young cricketers, stepping onto the lush outfield illuminated by tower lights felt just like walking onto an international stage. The cool night air and the glowing green turf brought an undeniable buzz of energy. Parents, coaches, and siblings bundled up along the boundary ropes, creating a warm, festive sideline atmosphere that echoed with cheers throughout the twenty overs.

Halton skipper Jai Singh called correctly at the coin toss and opted to bowl first, eager to test our bowling attack and ground-fielding under the night sky.

Sharp Bowling and Stellar Ground Fielding
Halton’s bowling unit came out firing from ball one, keeping NCC Academy on the back foot early. Yuvan Garg set the standard with a sensational double-strike in the second over, rattling the stumps of NCC opener Ved Patel and following up with another clean bowled to leave NCC reeling at 11/2. Yuvan finished an economical spell with impressive figures of 2 for 20 from his three overs.

The pressure never let up. Atharv Bansal delivered two very tight overs (1/12) and grabbed the big wicket of NCC captain Mahin Dave, courtesy of a sharp catch in the deep by Mirdhani Saravanakumar.

Halton’s fielding under the lights was sharp and composed, producing three outstanding run-outs: Atharv Bansal produced a direct-hit run-out to remove Josiah Ebenezer, Mirdhani Saravanakumar displayed quick reflexes to run out Krishna D, and Viraj Kaushik executed another alert dismissal to run out Yugma Patel.

Late in the innings, Nithisha Chakkaravarthi turned in a masterclass of control, bowling with great precision to claim 2 wickets for just 11 runs in three overs, including a plumb lbw and another clean bowled. Solid overs from Samar Multani (2 overs for 9 runs), Saibhang Singh, and Manbir Singh helped keep NCC Academy within reach at 127/8 in their 20 overs.

A Gritty Chase with Heart and Fight
Chasing 128, the Halton boys approached the challenge with courage against a disciplined NCC bowling attack. Opening batsman Sarmad Faraz played a delightful, confident knock, punching two boundaries and rotating the strike nicely on his way to a top-scoring 21 off 22 deliveries. He partnered with Manbir Singh (10 off 18 balls) to lay a solid foundation, guiding Halton past 50 in the 9th over.

Captain Jai Singh anchored the middle order with grit and determination. Demonstrating great patience against tight bowling, Jai remained unbeaten on 17 off 23 balls* (featuring 2 boundaries) and batted through the closing overs. Lower down the order, Viraj Kaushik provided late fireworks with a brisk 5 off just 4 balls* including a cracking boundary.

Despite our spirited efforts, NCC’s bowling trio struck at crucial moments, restricting Halton to 110/8 when the 20th over closed.

Lessons Learned and Memories Made
While NCC Academy took the win by 17 runs, the mood in the Halton camp was pure pride and joy. Adapting to night cricket—judging aerial balls against the night sky, reading bounce under artificial lighting, and managing game situations under the floodlights—is a massive leap in any junior player’s development.

The smiles on the kids’ faces and the shared laughs over hot snacks with parents post-match captured the true spirit of junior sport. Halton Cricket Academy walks away with heads held high, richer in experience, tighter as a team, and eager for their next night fixture.

Match Summary
Toss: Halton Cricket Academy opted to field.
NCC Academy: 127/8 in 20.0 overs — Nithisha Chakkaravarthi 2/11, Yuvan Garg 2/20, Atharv Bansal 1/12.
Halton Cricket Academy: 110/8 in 20.0 overs — Sarmad Faraz 21, Jai Singh 17*, Manbir Singh 10.
Result: NCC Academy won by 17 runs.
Venue: Niagara Cricket Centre, Niagara Falls, ON.

COMMUNITY ADVOCACY

Young Cricketers Step Up to the Pitch at Burlington City Hall

BURLINGTON, ON — Clad in their club jerseys, young athletes from the Halton Cricket Academy traded their bats and pads for civic dialogue this week, attending a City of Burlington public engagement session to meet directly with Mayor Marianne Meed Ward and members of City Council.

The delegation of youth players, coaches, and parents joined the open community forum to voice their passion for cricket—one of the fastest-growing youth sports across the Halton region—while gaining a behind-the-scenes look at how municipal government supports local recreation and public spaces.

Behind the Scenes of Municipal Governance
During the session, the young players engaged in an interactive discussion with city administrators and elected officials about the day-to-day operations of municipal government. The youth learned how city staff plan park usage, allocate maintenance budgets, and balance the needs of diverse recreational groups across Burlington’s parklands.

“It was eye-opening for our young players to see that safe, open spaces to play cricket don’t just happen on their own,” said one of the academy’s lead organizers. “They discovered the planning, permits, and municipal teamwork required across departments to keep our community spaces running smoothly.”

City council members commended the youth for stepping up to the microphone, asking thoughtful questions about local sports infrastructure, pitch availability, and long-term park development.

Champions of Clean, Safe Grounds
A major theme of the dialogue centered on park stewardship and safety. Municipal staff and council emphasized the shared civic responsibility required to maintain Burlington’s recreational fields — from field safety and pitch integrity (how divots, debris, and improper wear can create tripping hazards and compromise the safety of high-speed athletic matches), to environmental stewardship (the direct impact of litter on surrounding ecosystems and stormwater systems, reinforcing the principle of leaving fields cleaner than players found them), to civic partnership (the role user groups play in promptly reporting hazards, damaged amenities, and turf issues through Service Burlington).

Mayor Marianne Meed Ward praised the academy’s proactive community presence, highlighting the value of youth civic engagement. “Having our youth involved in local governance is how we build stronger, more vibrant communities,” Mayor Meed Ward noted during the meeting. “These young athletes demonstrated not only their passion for cricket, but also a genuine commitment to taking care of the public parks and facilities that belong to all of us.”

Building Community Leaders on and off the Field
For the Halton Cricket Academy, the visit served as an extension of the values taught on the pitch: discipline, respect, teamwork, and accountability. Academy coaches emphasized that learning how city hall operates helps develop well-rounded community ambassadors, not just skilled batsmen and bowlers.

The session concluded with a group photo on the council chamber floor, with the young athletes pledging to champion park cleanup initiatives and take active pride in preserving their home training grounds throughout the upcoming season.

PRE-SEASON

Halton Cricket Academy Gears Up for Early Season Start with April Pre-Season Fixtures in Hamilton

HAMILTON, ON — Halton Cricket Academy is hitting the pitch earlier than usual this spring, launching its competitive preparations with a series of pre-season friendly matches scheduled across Hamilton this April.

The early kickoff marks a deliberate push by academy coaching staff to transition players quickly from winter indoor nets to outdoor turf and pitch conditions. With traditional outdoor league play across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area typically peaking from late May through the summer, securing game action in April provides academy squads with a distinct competitive edge.

Sharpening Match Fitness Ahead of League Campaign
The upcoming fixtures in Hamilton will test squads across multiple age brackets, giving developing youth players and senior academy members invaluable match time. The series focuses on live-situation play: refining bowling rotations, adapting batting lineups against varied bowling attacks, and sharpening ground fielding and slip catching in open-field conditions.

“Indoor training in the winter is crucial for technical refinement, but nothing substitutes for reading natural ball trajectory, coping with variable wind conditions, and executing tactical communication on a full pitch,” notes the academy coaching team. “Getting outdoors in April helps shake off winter rust and accelerates game sense well before tournament play begins.”

Collaborative Regional Competition
Hamilton’s cricket facilities will serve as the battleground for the friendlies, bringing together local clubs and academy talent from across the Golden Horseshoe. The cross-regional matches serve two purposes: providing rigorous tactical tests for players and strengthening ties within Southern Ontario’s rapidly expanding grassroots cricket scene.

Key elements of the April pre-season schedule include simulated pressure scenarios — limited-overs formats designed to evaluate middle-order pacing and death-bowling execution; squad depth evaluation, with equal opportunity match play ensuring non-starting and developmental players receive substantive overs and innings under competitive conditions; and conditioning and turf adaptation, acclimating players to early spring temperatures and early-season outfield dynamics before standard league fixtures commence.

Looking Ahead to the Summer Slate
With registration and training rosters finalizing, academy officials expect the April series to set the tone for an ambitious summer calendar across regional youth leagues and invitational tournaments.

Supporters, parents, and local cricket enthusiasts can find match timings, pitch locations, and schedule updates directly through the academy’s communications channels prior to the opening weekend in April.
